import calendar
import datetime
from datetime import datetime as datetime_2

import pytest
from dateutil.relativedelta import MO, relativedelta


def test_relativedelta___init____dt1_dt2_datetime_diff_positive():
    dt1 = datetime.datetime(2022, 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 123456)
    dt2 = datetime.datetime(2020, 3, 5, 10, 20, 30, 654321)

    rd = relativedelta(dt1, dt2)

    # months delta = (2022-2020)*12 + (5-3) = 26 -> 2 years, 2 months
    assert rd.years == 2
    assert rd.months == 2
    # time components should be present and non‑negative
    assert rd._has_time == 1
    assert rd.seconds >= 0
    assert rd.microseconds >= 0
    # days should be non‑negative (the algorithm never makes days negative here)
    assert rd.days >= 0


def test_relativedelta___repr____repr_mixed():
    """Calling repr on a relativedelta with both relative and absolute attributes."""
    rd = relativedelta(years=2, month=7, day=15, weekday=MO)
    # Relative part first (years), then absolute parts in defined order
    expected = "relativedelta(years=+2, month=7, day=15, weekday=MO)"
    assert repr(rd) == expected


def test_relativedelta_normalized__normalize_large_float_days_multiple_casc():
    # Large fractional days that cascade through hours, minutes, seconds, microseconds
    rd = relativedelta(days=2.999999)
    norm = rd.normalized()
    assert norm.days == 2
    assert norm.hours == 23
    assert norm.minutes == 59
    assert norm.seconds == 59
    # Remaining fraction after seconds: 0.9136 → 913600 microseconds
    assert norm.microseconds == 913600


def test_relativedelta___init____relative_args_positive_integers():
    rd = relativedelta(
        years=1,
        months=14,          # will overflow to an extra year
        days=3,
        hours=5,
        minutes=120,        # 2 extra hours
        seconds=3661,       # 1 hour, 1 minute, 1 second
        microseconds=2_000_000  # 2 extra seconds
    )

    # Normalisation performed by _fix()
    assert rd.years == 2          # 1 + overflow from months
    assert rd.months == 2          # 14 -> 1 year + 2 months
    assert rd.days == 3
    # Hours: 5 + 2 (from minutes) + 1 (from seconds) = 8
    assert rd.hours == 8
    # Minutes: 120 -> 0, plus 1 from seconds overflow = 1
    assert rd.minutes == 1
    # Seconds: 3661 + 2 (from microseconds) = 3663 -> 3 after overflow
    assert rd.seconds == 3
    # Microseconds normalised to 0
    assert rd.microseconds == 0
    # No absolute fields were supplied
    assert rd.year is None and rd.month is None and rd.day is None
    assert rd._has_time == 1

def test_relativedelta___add____cover_weekday():

    result = rd + start

    # Monday after 2021-05-05 is 2021-05-10
    expected = datetime.datetime(2021, 5, 10, 0, 0, 0)
    assert isinstance(result, datetime.datetime)
    assert result == expected

def test_relativedelta_normalized__normalize_negative_floats_cascade():
    # Negative fractional values that should cascade down the units
    rd = relativedelta(days=-1.7, hours=-3.2, minutes=-4.5, seconds=-5.6, microseconds=-250000.7)
    norm = rd.normalized()
    assert norm.days == -1
    assert norm.hours == -20
    assert norm.minutes == -4
    assert norm.seconds == -35
    # -5.6 seconds + (-0.5 minute) → -35.6 seconds, fractional -0.6 → -600000 microseconds
    # original -250000.7 + (-600000) = -850000.7 → round → -850001
    assert norm.microseconds == -850001

def test_relativedelta___init____relative_args_weeks_leapdays_yearday():
    rd = relativedelta(
        weeks=2,          # 14 days
        leapdays=1,       # will be overridden by yearday logic
        yearday=60        # 60th day of year -> March 1 according to implementation
    )

    # weeks contribute to days
    assert rd.days == 14
    # yearday conversion sets month/day (implementation yields March 1)
    assert rd.month == 3
    assert rd.day == 1
    # because yearday > 59, leapdays is forced to -1
    assert rd.leapdays == -1
    # No time component
    assert rd._has_time == 0


def test_relativedelta___init____dt1_dt2_mixed_types_coercion():

    dt2 = datetime.date(2022, 3, 10)          # date, no time

    rd = relativedelta(dt1, dt2)

    # The date should have been coerced to a midnight datetime.
    # Expected delta: 5 days + 12 hours.
    assert rd.days == 5
    assert rd.hours == 12
    assert rd.seconds == 0
    assert rd.microseconds == 0
    assert rd._has_time == 1


def test_relativedelta___init____dt1_dt2_date_diff_negative():
    dt1 = datetime.date(2020, 1, 1)
    dt2 = datetime.date(2020, 1, 10)

    rd = relativedelta(dt1, dt2)

    # No month/year offset
    assert rd.years == 0
    assert rd.months == 0
    # The negative offset is represented in the days attribute after normalization
    assert rd.days == -9
    # Seconds and microseconds are normalized to zero
    assert rd.seconds == 0
    assert rd.microseconds == 0
    # No time component was supplied
    assert rd._has_time == 0

        seconds=59,
        minutes=59,
        months=11,
        microseconds=1000000
    )
    rd_other = relativedelta(year=2025, month=12, day=25)
    result = rd_self + rd_other

    assert isinstance(result, relativedelta)
    # relative years are summed
    assert result.years == 1
    # relative months sum
    assert result.months == 11
    # relative days sum
    assert result.days == 0
    # relative time fields after normalization
    assert result.hours == 1
    assert result.minutes == 0
    assert result.seconds == 0
    assert result.microseconds == 0
    # absolute overrides from other
    assert result.year == 2025
    assert result.month == 12
    assert result.day == 25


def test_relativedelta___add____add_datetime_object_relative_only():
    rd = relativedelta(years=1, months=2, days=10, hours=5, minutes=30)
    dt = datetime.datetime(2020, 1, 31, 12, 0, 0)
    result = rd + dt

    # Expected: year 2021, month March (1+2), day min(31,10)=10, then +10 days = 20th
    expected = datetime.datetime(2021, 4, 10, 17, 30, 0)
    assert isinstance(result, datetime.datetime)
    assert result == expected


def test_relativedelta_weeks_setter__set_weeks_negative_from_positive_days():
    rd = relativedelta(days=21)
    rd.weeks = -2
    assert rd.days == -14


def test_relativedelta___radd____radd_datetime_object_with_weekday():
    dt = datetime.datetime(2023, 1, 1)
    rd = relativedelta(weekday=calendar.THURSDAY)
    result = dt + rd
    assert result == datetime.datetime(2023, 1, 5)


def test_relativedelta___rsub____rsub_mixed_rd_from_datetime():
    dt = datetime_2(2023, 1, 1)
    rd = relativedelta(years=1, months=-2, days=3)
    result = dt - rd
    assert result == datetime_2(2022, 2, 26)


def test_relativedelta___bool____bool_mixed_components():
    delta = relativedelta(years=1, month=2, day=None, weekday=(calendar.MONDAY, 1))
    assert bool(delta)


def test_relativedelta___hash____hash_different_objects():
    delta1 = relativedelta(years=2, months=3, days=4)
    delta2 = relativedelta(years=2, months=3, days=5)

    # Build the tuples that __hash__ hashes
    t1 = (None, 2, 3, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0,
          None, None, None, None, None, None, None)
    t2 = (None, 2, 3, 5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0,
          None, None, None, None, None, None, None)

    # Expected hash values derived from the tuples (independent of the code under test)
    expected1 = hash(t1)
    expected2 = hash(t2)

    # Verify that __hash__ produces the expected values
    assert hash(delta1) == expected1
    assert hash(delta2) == expected2

    # Ensure the two different instances yield different hash values
    assert expected1 != expected2
